subject: chemistry
title: Titration calculations
key_idea: (Separate chemistry) A titration finds the volumes of an acid and an alkali that react exactly. (AQA: Higher tier) Find the moles of the solution you know, use the equation ratio to get the moles of the other, then divide by its volume.

blocks.text: A titration measures the volume of one solution needed to react completely with a fixed volume of another. This section covers how it is done and which results to use.

items.meaning: A method to find the volumes of two solutions that react exactly, using an indicator.
The volume added from the burette, read from the burette scale.
Titres within 0.10 cm³ of each other.

diagram.alt: Put the steps of a titration into the correct order.
steps: Use a pipette to put 25.0 cm³ of alkali into a conical flask
Add a few drops of indicator
Fill the burette with acid and read the starting volume
Add the acid, swirling the flask, and go drop by drop near the end
Read the final volume from the burette and repeat

items: Stand the flask on a white tile to see the colour change clearly.
Use an indicator with a sharp colour change, such as phenolphthalein or methyl orange. Universal indicator changes colour too gradually.
A rough first titration shows roughly where the end point is.
Repeat the titration until you have concordant results.
Ignore any result that is not concordant, such as a rough first titration.
Use the **mean** of the concordant titres in the calculation.
Add acid, drop by drop near the end, until the indicator just changes colour.
Use the mean of the concordant titres.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) The calculation always follows the same four steps. The equation ratio links the two solutions.

blocks.label: Moles in a solution
where: Divide the volume in cm³ by 1000 to get dm³.

items.text: Titres: 23.50, 21.10, 22.10, 22.15, 22.15. The last three are within 0.10 cm³. The mean is 22.13 cm³.
2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. The ratio is 2 NaOH : 1 H₂SO₄, so moles of H₂SO₄ = 0.002324 ÷ 2 = 0.001162 mol.
The acid volume is 25.0 cm³. 0.001162 × 1000 ÷ 25.0 = 0.0465 mol/dm³.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the concentration of sulfuric acid from a titration result.
working: Ratio H₂SO₄ : NaOH = 1 : 2, so moles of H₂SO₄ = moles of NaOH ÷ 2
diagram.question: 25.0 cm³ of sulfuric acid is neutralised by **{V} cm³** of 0.200 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide solution. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid in mol/dm³.

items: Use the ratio from the equation to change moles.
Divide the moles by the volume (dm³) of the unknown solution.

sections.heading: Other things the titration can find

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) The same method can find a volume, or a concentration in g/dm³.

items: To find a volume: find the moles needed, then volume = moles ÷ concentration. For 0.003 mol of NaOH at 0.4 mol/dm³: 0.003 ÷ 0.4 = 0.0075 dm³ = 7.5 cm³.
To give g/dm³, multiply the concentration in mol/dm³ by Mr. For H₂SO₄ at 0.048 mol/dm³ (Mr = 98): 0.048 × 98 = 4.7 g/dm³.
Check the units and significant figures asked for.

checks.q: What is meant by concordant results?
checks.a: Titres that are within 0.10 cm³ of each other.

checks.q: 25.0 cm³ of 0.124 mol/dm³ sodium carbonate is neutralised by 23.6 cm³ of nitric acid: Na₂CO₃ + 2HNO₃ → 2NaNO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the nitric acid to 3 significant figures.
Why is the volume of the titre divided by 1000 in the calculation?
checks.a: To convert cm³ to dm³, because concentration is in mol/dm³.

worked_example.question:
A student titrated 25.0 cm³ portions of dilute sulfuric acid with a 0.105 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide solution.

Volume of sodium hydroxide solution used:
Titration 1: 23.50 cm³
Titration 2: 21.10 cm³
Titration 3: 22.10 cm³
Titration 4: 22.15 cm³
Titration 5: 22.15 cm³

The equation for the reaction is: 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O

Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid in mol/dm³.

Use only the student's concordant results.

Concordant results are those within 0.10 cm³ of each other.
worked_example.tip: Marks follow your own working, so a mistake in one step does not lose the later marks.

worked_example.question:
In another titration 25.0 cm³ of potassium hydroxide solution, KOH, are titrated with 0.200 mol / dm³ sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄.

2KOH + H₂SO₄ → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O

24.80 cm³ of sulfuric acid are needed to neutralise 25.0 cm³ of the potassium hydroxide solution.

Calculate the concentration of the potassium hydroxide solution in mol / dm³.
answer_points: Concentration of KOH = 0.00992 × 1000 ÷ 25.0 = 0.3968 mol / dm³, or 0.40 (2)
worked_example.tip: 0.3968, 0.397 and 0.40 are all accepted. The unit is not needed on the answer line.

worked_example.question:
25.0 cm³ of aqueous sodium hydroxide, NaOH, of concentration 0.100 mol/dm³ is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of dilute sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄.

The equation for the reaction is shown.

2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O

Calculate the concentration of H₂SO₄ using the following steps.
● Calculate the number of moles of NaOH used.
● Determine the number of moles of H₂SO₄ that react with the NaOH.
● Calculate the concentration of H₂SO₄.
